result.title: Learning Deployable Causal Action Geometry under Temporal Non-Stationarity
result.summary: Learning a response law for continuous decisions from observational time series is central to many real-world decision systems, yet temporal non-stationarity poses a fundamental challenge: as outcomes drift over time, naively pooled models can conflate action effects with shifting baselines and even reverse action rankings. Even when the one-step response is identifiable, unrestricted cross-time generalization remains fundamentally ill-posed. We therefore seek the part of the response that remains stable for decisions even when outcome levels do not. We propose deployable causal action geometry: the action-response shape that remains after anchoring away action-independent level shifts on a selected link scale and profiling out positive amplitude variation. Building on this target, we develop a two-stage orthogonal estimator that first obtains cross-fitted pilot estimates of anchored responses and then performs honest profiled selection over link, representation, and shape classes. The resulting estimator admits oracle guarantees for the restricted target and, under approximate persistence, produces decision rules that remain near optimal in future periods. Experiments on synthetic data and Dominick's support the proposed target and its transfer behavior. In a randomized Taobao A/B test, the deployed system improves GMV and purchase counts by \(1.16\%\) and \(1.70\%\).

AI.brief_summary: 面向时间非平稳下的连续决策，提出「可部署因果动作几何」这一去除了水平漂移与幅度变化的响应形状目标，并用两阶段正交估计器在链接、表示与形状类上做诚实筛选，在合成数据、Dominick's 与淘宝 A/B 实验中验证迁移与决策收益。
AI.relevance_reason: 属因果推断与决策/计量经济方向，讨论的是动作效应在时间漂移下的稳定响应形状，未涉及多模态内部状态、视觉证据使用或 latent 推理生成，也无可核查的表示或状态更新借鉴线索，故排除。
